explanation: Lead is more reactive than copper, so it displaces copper from copper chloride solution, forming lead chloride and metallic copper.

beaker_view.initial_appearance: A grey lead strip dropped into a green to blue-green copper chloride solution.
beaker_view.final_appearance: A pale, near-colourless lead chloride solution (lead chloride is only sparingly soluble, so some may appear as a fine white precipitate), with the lead strip coated in reddish-brown copper.
beaker_view.observation: The green solution fades as the lead strip picks up a reddish copper coating — though this exact pairing is less commonly demonstrated than the iron or zinc versions, so treat the shade of green and whether a visible white precipitate forms as the less certain part of this one.
